devdoc.details: The integer id is only unique within one registry deployment on one chain — off-chain consumers must key groups by (chainId, registryAddress, groupId). TRUST MODEL: attaching a group to any consumer (e.g. WhitelistPreIntentHookV2) delegates ongoing admission policy to the group's controller set: the current owner, any future owner after transfer, and the current and any future resolver. Any of these can admit arbitrary accounts at any time.

params._name: Human-readable label, emitted in the event only (not stored).

params._newOwner: Proposed new owner (must be nonzero; cancellation is a dedicated function).

devdoc.title: AddressGroupRegistry

acceptGroupOwnership(uint256).notice: Completes a pending ownership transfer. Callable only by the pending owner. The previous owner retains no access after acceptance.

addMembers(uint256,address[]).notice: Adds members to a group. Idempotent: already-present members are skipped (no event).

createGroup(string).notice: Creates a new group owned by the caller.

getGroup(uint256).notice: Returns a group's governance state for atomic inspection.

groupCount().notice: Returns the last assigned group id (ids start at 1).

groupExists(uint256).notice: Returns whether a group exists (input validation only — not a trust guarantee).

isMember(uint256,address).notice: Returns whether an account is a member of a group (curated OR resolver). Returns false for nonexistent groups. Resolver failures fail closed for that resolver only — they never revert this call.

removeMembers(uint256,address[]).notice: Removes members from a group. Idempotent: absent members are skipped (no event).

setResolver(uint256,address).notice: Sets or clears the group's resolver. A nonzero resolver must have code; note this does not make upgradeable or malicious resolvers safe — the resolver is part of the group's trust surface.

transferGroupOwnership(uint256,address).notice: Starts a two-step ownership transfer. Replaces any existing pending owner.

userdoc.notice: Permissionless registry of owner-managed address groups. Groups are identified by a sequential uint256 id (starting at 1) and are never deleted. Only the group owner mutates members and the resolver; shared control is achieved by using a multisig as the owner.
